paper_summary.rationale: Cost-effective ($0.15/$0.6 per 1M tokens) with excellent quality for structured summaries. 128K context window handles full papers.

selection_summary.rationale: Fast and cost-effective for short inline summaries. Balances speed and quality.

qa.rationale: Excellent reasoning capabilities at low cost. Good for grounded Q&A with citations.

default.rationale: Default fallback model for any task type not explicitly configured.

paper_summary.rationale: Most cost-effective option ($0.25/$1.25 per 1M tokens). Fast with 200K context window. Excellent for high-volume summarization.

selection_summary.rationale: Ultra-fast and cheap for inline summaries. Perfect for quick context extraction.

qa.rationale: Best reasoning capabilities for complex Q&A. Higher cost but superior for understanding nuanced research questions.

paper_summary.rationale: Excellent for long documents with 1M token context. Cost-effective ($0.075/$0.3 per 1M tokens) for paper summarization.

selection_summary.rationale: Fast and very cheap. Ideal for quick inline summaries.

qa.rationale: Better reasoning for complex Q&A tasks. Higher quality responses for research questions.

paper_summary.rationale: Chosen by measurement, not reputation. On a real 13.8kB payload from an ingested paper it returned 5 key findings in 8s. nemotron-3-super returned valid JSON with an EMPTY findings array on the same input — a silent no-op that is worse than an error. 1M context also fits a whole paper without truncation.

selection_summary.rationale: A selection summary is short and bounded, and super handles that fine (2 bullets in 7.2s) — its weakness only showed on full-paper input. Kept distinct from the qa/summary model so the three tasks do not share one free-tier rate limit.

qa.rationale: Fastest and highest quality of the free models actually tested against this app's JSON-schema calls (3s short, 8s long). Q&A is where grounding quality matters most.

default.rationale: Default fallback - free tier on OpenRouter.

notes.selection_strategy: Models chosen based on cost-effectiveness and task-specific requirements. Summarization tasks prioritize cost while Q&A prioritizes reasoning quality.
notes.customization: Override specific models by setting environment variables: {PROVIDER}_{TASK}_MODEL (e.g., OPENAI_QA_MODEL=gpt-4o)
notes.openrouter_free_tier: OpenRouter rotates and retires :free slugs without notice — every model configured here before 2026-07-29 returned 404. If summarize or qa fail with a 404 naming a paid slug, re-check https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models for current :free ids rather than assuming a code fault.
notes.openrouter_model_selection: Pick on two measured properties, not on parameter count or blog rankings. (1) The model must honour response_format json_schema — this app calls generateJson everywhere. The catalogue's supported_parameters field is unreliable in BOTH directions: openai/gpt-oss-20b advertises structured_outputs and returns ```json-fenced markdown, while nemotron-3-ultra advertises neither and complies correctly. (2) It must still do the work on a realistic payload. nemotron-3-super passes a toy prompt but returns an empty findings array on a real 13.8kB paper. Always test with real chunk text.
